text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu expected to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat today.
- U.S.: Iraqi withdrawal from Kurdish region is insignificant.
- Jerusalem Mayor Ehud Olmert warns Palestinian Authority to stay away from Jerusalem schools.
- Government discusses plan for Gaza industrial park.
- Finance Committee opposes proposed cut in small business aid.
HAARETZ
- Palestinian source: Netanyahu and Arafat will apparently meet today. Israel: meeting not set yet.
- Clinton will decide in next 24 hours which military option to use against Iraq.
- Former Likud Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir: Why was there a power change if we're ready to agree to a Palestinian state?
- Tax collection arrears worsen: 3.5 billion shekels in 1996.
- Bank of Israel again stops daily monetary tenders.
MAARIV
- Senior political officials in Jerusalem: 'If there are no surprises Netanyahu and Arafat will meet today.'
- Former Turkish Prime Minister Elmaz: 'Israel protested 10 days ago against Iraqi intrusions to Kurdistan'.
- Slain Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin's son Yuval: Labour party leader Shimon Peres needs to draw conclusions and quit.
- Suspicion of rebellion against Netanyahu in Likud party.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu-Arafat meeting expected to take place today. Main obstacle to holding the meeting: Israel demands alterations to Hebron redeployment.
- Majority in government favour Netanyahu-Arafat meeting: eight ministers for, five abstain, two against.
- Government hopes to privatise companies and banks for 6 billion shekels in 1997.
GLOBES
- Economic officials: reasonable chances of lowering Israel's credit rating.
- External experts in monetary council to be appointed or approved only by Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel.
- Real decline of 3 percent in August tax inflows.
